correctness.rationale: The proof verifies both implication directions of exact reachability, including the critical initial-run merger case for a removable unmatched singleton second run. Counting all embeddings once via greedy subsequence matching yields the exact binomial difference at every n>=1,t>=0, also r=n. Polynomial binomial tails prove fixed-seed asymptotic density. A stand-alone program directly enumerated 2,550 seed/radius pairs and checked 84,490 inverse lemmas; finite checks are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The earlier exact REGULAR LANGUAGE factorization covers unbounded reachability and is acknowledged. Counting distinct members of every fixed-length layer after arbitrary overlapping generation histories is a separate enumerative problem. The checked papers and four semantic searches do not state the closed binomial sphere law, its dependence only on the initial seed run, or the sharp extreme/density consequences. Subsequence binomial counts are standard and explicitly credited. Residual risk includes equivalent enumeration implicit in regular-language methods.
residual_risks: The known entire descendant regular language logically determines each finite-radius coefficient; alternate literature may already have carried out this counting under a different name.

value.rationale: Distinct forward sphere volume at every finite error radius is a natural coding/storage invariant for the well-established reverse-complement duplication channel. The closed two-parameter law eliminates history multiplicity and shows all later seed content is irrelevant: a robust structural simplification, sharp extremes, and asymptotic densities. This is not merely a cheap normalization or a known first-step count.
